## Hinge question · What do we know? {#iv5-direction-hinge .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .geometric-lesson}

<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="4" class="hinge numeric-choices">
<p class="hinge-question">Given <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=6"></span>, <span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{a}|=3"></span> and <span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{b}|=4"></span>, which statement describes the two vectors?</p>
<div class="hinge-toolbar"><div class="time" role="timer" aria-label="Time remaining">1:00</div><div class="toolbar"><label>Seconds <select class="timer-duration" aria-label="Question duration"><option>30</option><option>45</option><option selected>60</option><option>90</option><option>120</option></select></label><button class="timer-start primary">Start</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div></div>
<div class="choices">
<button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span>Same direction</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span>Opposite directions</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span>Perpendicular</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span>Neither parallel nor perpendicular</span></button>
</div>
<div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly.<br>On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div>
<div class="hinge-explanation" hidden><strong>4.</strong> <span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|=12"></span>. Same direction requires a scalar product of <span data-math="12"></span>, opposite directions <span data-math="-12"></span>, and perpendicular vectors <span data-math="0"></span>. The given value is <span data-math="6"></span>, so none applies.</div>
</div>

::: notes
Immediately after Example 5.4. Correct choice 4: neither parallel nor perpendicular. Magnitudes 3 and 4 give |a||b|=12, so the three special values are 12,−12,0; the supplied dot product 6 is none of these. Choice 1 is the key misconception: positive does not necessarily mean the same direction. Choice 2 would require −12, not merely a non-zero dot product. Choice 3 would require zero. Students can decide without calculating the angle, which belongs to Lesson 6. Default 60 seconds, adjustable; no automatic answer reveal. Use simultaneous 1–4 finger responses. Ready: proceed to Key Ideas. Divided: compare the given result with the three special values and revote. Needs explanation: return to the sign activity with lengths 2 and 5; compare 60° (positive product 5) with 0° (product 10). Reaffirm that a positive dot product identifies an acute angle, or the zero-degree endpoint, rather than necessarily parallel vectors.
:::
